messages:
Marta (CS): heads-up — AcmeCorp reported SCIM provisioning creating users but not assigning the expected product roles. they say group sync from their IdP (Okta) shows success on their side but our dashboard shows users in 'default' role. can anyone triage? :confused:
Devon (Eng): grabbing logs now. which org id / example user?
Marta (CS): org: acct-acmecorp, example user: laura.t@acme.com. customer paste says SCIM logs show a 401 on /scim/v2/Groups import about halfway through sync window.
Devon (Eng): okay pasting the redwood side error snippet we see when group sync runs: 
```
2026-02-25T15:22:41Z ERROR scim.sync: /scim/v2/Groups import failed status=401 body={"error":"insufficient_scope","error_description":"The OAuth token does not grant scim.write scope"}
```
Devon (Eng): so looks like the token used by their IdP connector is missing the scim.write or scim.manage scope. that would let group-to-role mappings apply.
Marta (CS): customer says they rotated their token yesterday. could be the new token was created with limited scopes by mistake. they also mentioned some groups had weird casing — "SRE-Admins" vs "sre-admins" — could mapping be case-sensitive?
Sanjay (Security): SCIM group matching in our mapping is case-sensitive by default. we can do case-insensitive patterns but that needs explicit regex in the mapping config. also older tokens issued to the same client id can be revoked automatically depending on IdP.
Devon (Eng): repro steps i used locally:
1) simulate Okta POST to /redwood/scim/oauth/token with client creds -> receive access_token with scopes: [openid profile]
2) attempt POST /scim/v2/Groups/import -> 401 insufficient_scope
3) update token to include scim.manage -> POST succeeds and groups are created with roles assigned via mapping.
Marta (CS): can you paste the minimal curl we used to validate? customer asked for exact command to run.
Devon (Eng): sure:
```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/scim/v2/Groups/import\" \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/scim+json\" \ 
  -d \"{}\"
```
if the token lacks scim.manage you'll get the 401 shown earlier.
Devon (Eng): also here's an example mapping snippet (their mapping currently):
```json
{"groupToRoleMapping": [{"groupName": "SRE-Admins","role": "admin"},{"groupName": "readers","role": "viewer"}],"caseSensitive": true}
```
Devon (Eng): because caseSensitive=true, "sre-admins" won't match "SRE-Admins". changing to caseSensitive=false or using a regex like `(?i)sre-admins` fixes it.
Marta (CS): customer is also upset because deprovisioning didn't remove billing seat quickly — they removed users in Okta but users still show active for 12+ hours here. any idea?
Sanjay (Security): check that their SCIM deprovision webhook is hitting /scim/v2/Users with method DELETE/PATCH correctly. we also have a config flag `preserve_roles_on_deprovision` which, if true, keeps roles/entitlements for auditing; default used to be true in older org configs. if their org was created before the change, it might be on.
Devon (Eng): logs show Okta sent the DELETE event and we processed it, but the downstream job that cleans up entitlements failed due to a transient DB deadlock at 15:25:02. snippet: 
```
ERROR serv.job: cleanup_entitlements job failed: pq: deadlock detected
```
Devon (Eng): job retried but their org's config had preserve_roles_on_deprovision=true so even a successful cleanup job wouldn't have removed roles.
Marta (CS): so two issues: token scope + case sensitivity causing missing role assignment, and preserve_roles_on_deprovision causing delayed seat release. customer wants an action plan and short-term remediation.
Devon (Eng): short-term remediation steps to give customer: 
- Ask their IdP admin to re-issue the OAuth token with scopes: `scim.manage scim.read scim.write` (scim.manage is the one that allows importing groups/role application). verify via token introspection or `jwt.io` if it's JWT.
- Re-run the `Groups/import` curl after token is rotated. that will apply mappings for existing groups.
- If group names vary only by case, either update IdP group names to match mapping or set `caseSensitive` to false in their mapping. example update API:
```bash
curl -X PATCH \"https://api.redwood.ai/orgs/acct-acmecorp/scim/mapping\" \ 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \ 
 -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
 -d '{"caseSensitive": false}'
```
- For deprovisioning, temporarily run a manual cleanup job (we can trigger from ops) and flip `preserve_roles_on_deprovision` to false if they want immediate seat release.
Marta (CS): can ops trigger the manual cleanup? customer wants it within the hour.
Sanjay (Security): ops-bot — can we run a manual entitlement cleanup for acct-acmecorp and confirm token scope check?
ops-bot: running cleanup job for org acct-acmecorp. this may take up to 2 minutes. :gear:
ops-bot: cleanup job started (job_id=cleanup-1771234589)
ops-bot: cleanup job completed successfully, removed 24 stale entitlements, took 31s. :white_check_mark:
Devon (Eng): i also pushed a one-off mapping change to their org to make caseSensitive=false and re-ran the import. verified via API that Laura now has role=admin.
Marta (CS): customer confirmed Laura sees admin in product now and seats decreased by 24. they're happy but want a write-up of what happened and recommended config.
Devon (Eng): will draft postmortem note and recommended config snippet: 
```json
{"recommendedScopes": ["scim.manage","scim.read","scim.write"],"recommendedMapping": {"caseSensitive": false},"notes": "Ensure tokens issued by IdP include scim.manage; prefer regex mapping for fuzzy matches."}
```
Marta (CS): perfect. i'll send to customer and close the ticket once they ack. thanks all. :tada:
Sanjay (Security): follow-up: i'll add a short UI validation to warn org admins if their SCIM token lacks scim.manage during connector setup. filing a small ticket.
Devon (Eng): nice — we should also log a clearer error string on 401 to show missing scope. created ENG-3109.
Marta (CS): closing thread, will update if customer re-opens. thanks everyone. :tada:
